title: Some People Are Young and Nothing More...
text:
Some people are young and nothing more

some people are old and nothing more.

And some people are in the middle

only in the middle.

And if flies wore clothes

and all the buildings burned in

golden fire,

if the sky shook like

a belly dance

and all the atomic bombs began to

scream,

some people would be young and nothing more

and some people would be old and nothing more

and the rest would be the same,

the rest would be the same.

The few who are different

are eliminated pretty quickly

by the police, by their mothers, their

brothers, and others

by themselves.

What remains is what

you see

it is hard.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the flat repetition and the hard closing diagnosis of ordinary sameness.

title: Culmination of Pain
text:
I even hear how

the mountains laugh

up and down their blue slopes

and down in the water

the fish weep

and all the water

is their tears.

I hear the water

the nights I consume drinking

and the sadness grows so large

that I hear it in my watch

it becomes knobs on the dresser,

it becomes paper on the floor,

it becomes shoehorn,

laundry ticket,

it becomes cigarette smoke

climbing a temple of dark vines...

Little matters,

little love

or little life

is not so bad.

What counts

is watching the walls

I was born for that.

I was born to steal roses from the avenues of death.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the expanding sadness, ordinary objects, and final rose-theft from death.

title: My Cats
text:
I know. I know.

they are limited, they have needs

and concerns

that are different.


but I watch them and learn from them.

I like how little they know,

which is

so much.


they complain but they never

worry.

they walk with astonishing dignity.

they sleep with a direct simplicity that

human beings simply cannot

understand.


their eyes are more

beautiful than ours.

and they can sleep 20 hours

a day

without hesitation or

remorse.


when I feel

low in spirits

all I need is

to watch my cats

and

courage

returns to me.


I study these

creatures


they are my

teachers.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Bukowski's admiration for cats as calm, dignified teachers.

title: Beans with Garlic
text:
This is fairly important

putting your feelings in writing

is better than shaving

or cooking beans with garlic

it is the little we can do

this small courage of knowledge

and there is also, of course,

the madness and terror

of knowing

that some part of you

is like a clock

that cannot be wound

again,

once it stops.

But now there is a tick-tock under your shirt

and you stir the beans with a spoon,

a dead love, a love that left,

another love...

ah!, as many loves as beans

yes, count them now

sad, sad

your feelings boiling over the flame

swallow this.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the comparison between writing, cooking, mortality, and feelings boiling like beans.
